27
OBSERV ATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
The Committee notes that during Eleventh Plan period, the Ministry of Tourism
could spend Rs.4896 crore out of the Rs.4953 crore allocated at RE, which is almost 98%
of the total allocations. The Committee also notes that the Ministry of Tourism has
sanctioned 1226 tourism projects for an amount of Rs.4090 crore during the Eleven Five
Year Plan. But the Committee was not informed about the completion of these projects or
the current status of these projects. It hopes that after sanctioning the projects and
releasing the money, the Ministry of Tourism is monitoring its implementation by the State
Governments. It is learnt that the State Governments are diverting these funds according
to their own priority. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should actively pursue
each of these projects sanctioned to ensure that the sanctioned amount is utilized in the
prescribed manner for the approved project only. (Para 10)
The Committee observes that under these schemes, Union territories appear to have
been neglected as the data shows that very few projects were sanctioned to them. For
example, Lakshadweep–1, Daman and Diu–l, Dadra and Nagar Haveli–3, and nothing for
Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The exceptions were Puducherry–20 and Chandigarh–11. If
non receipt of the proposal has been the reason, the Committee recommends that the
Ministry of Tourism should guide and encourage these union territories to submit viable
projects so that they may also get the fund allocations under these very important schemes.
These areas have ample potential for tourism development. (Para 11)
The Committee also appreciates the NE-States on their eagerness in implementing
tourism projects during the Eleventh Plan period. All the NE States have got good amount
of allocations and that Committee hopes that all these projects are being implemented
earnestly and timely. This will increase the tourist visits in this region which will improve
their over all economic condition in the coming years. (Para 12)
The Committee also observes that bigger States having immense potential for
tourism development, particularly pilgrimage, wild life and niche tourism, have not had
commensurate projects funds under these schemes. The Committee recommends that more
attention should be given during Twelfth Plan to those States which were yet to exploit their
potential for tourism development. (Para 13)
ANALYSIS OF BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS 2012-13 AND 2013-14
This Committee has always been arguing the case of Ministry of Tourism for
enhanced allocations every year during the examination of its Demands for Grants. The
Planning Commission, however, appears to have been reluctant to do so for reasons best
known to it. Normally, it does not give any reasons for this to a Ministry. During current
year also, only Rs.1282.00 crore has been allocated to the  Ministry against a projected
demand of Rs.1773.79 crore. The Committee, keeping in view the various targets fixed for
development and promotion of tourism infrastructure, creating skilled and trained
manpower, exploring new tourism projects etc, reiterates its recommendation for providing
additional funds to the Ministry of Tourism so that the ideal of linking tourism with
employment generation and poverty alleviation could be achieved in reality. (Para 20)

28
The Committee notes that during the Eleventh Plan period, right from the opening
years, the spending had remained more than 98%. However, in the opening year (2012-13)
of the Twelfth Plan, the spending pattern had not been so. The BE 2012-13 stood at Rs.1210
crores which was reduced at the RE to Rs.9S0 crore. But only Rs.724.34 crore could be spent
upto February, 2013. If this spending is analyzed on the basis of the BE allocation of
Rs.1210 crore during the period, it forms only 60% of it. The Committee feels that there
are failures on the part of the Ministry in dealing with plan schemes whatever be the
adverse policy changes. The Ministry should have taken up the matter at the appropriate
Governmental levels, rather than blaming the system. The Committee recommends that
Ministry of Tourism needs to be more proactive and work as facilitator for implementation
of its schemes. (Para 21)
The Committee notes that the Ministry has not projected their achievement in
measurable terms by providing required information in quantified and comparable format to
the Committee. That would have helped the Committee to understand and appreciate the
real problems before the Ministry and concretize its opinion accordingly. Next time the
Committee would like to have information in user friendly format for its purpose.
(Para 22)
The Committee also notes that some of the schemes such as incentives to
accommodation, assistance to large revenue generating projects, creation of land banks, etc.
are languishing for many years. The Committee recommends that these schemes may be
reviewed so that it may accomplish its targets. (Para 23)
The Committee observes that the strict guidelines on adherence to the utilization
certificate of each projects and further allocation of funds strictly thereafter has been able
to bring some accountability and discipline in the spending pattern of the Ministry. However,
the Committee is of the opinion that such measures should be based on practical
consideration as the infrastructure projects are required to get various sanctions/clearances
from so many agencies under different Ministries. Usually, the projects, involving land
acquisition and environment clearance are the most time consuming. Therefore, keeping all
these matters in mind, if the interpretation of rules/guidelines on fund disbursement
scheme has posed any problem to the ministries, it should be taken up at appropriate levels
and resolved as soon as possible. (Para 24)
The Committee notes that the Twelfth Plan has given emphasis to rural tourism and
projected tourism as a tool to reduce poverty. The Committee, however, finds no special
schemes or efforts to promote the rural tourism or spread the idea of tourism as a mass
activity. The Committee notes in the Budget 2013-14, just routine programmes which are
going on for the last so many years. (Para 25)
The Committee is also of the view that the plans and programmes of the Ministry
of Tourism should be aimed at positioning tourism as a major contributor of economic
growth and harness its direct and multiplier effects for employment and poverty eradication
in an environmentally sustainable manner. The schemes taken up by the Ministry should
be aimed at enhancing employment in the activities relating to tourism sector as well as at
fostering economic integration through developing linkages with other sectors. (Para 26)
The Committee further recommends that with the aim to achieve socio-economic
development in rural areas which have core competence in arts, crafts, heritage etc., the
Ministry of Tourism should provide assistance for development of tourism infrastructure and
capacity building of rural inhabitants in the States. The Ministry need to pursue with the

29
State Governments for completion of rural tourism projects sanctioned in a particular
financial year within a fixed time-frame. (Para 27)
PRODUCT/INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT FOR DESTINATIONS AND CIRCUITS
The Committee notes that allocations for PIDDC scheme are getting reduced as compared
to allocations made during 2011-12 and 2012-13. The Committee also notes that current year
allocation stands further reduced at Rs.400 crore. The Committee thus finds a regular
reduction in allocation from the 2011-12 onwards. A re-interpretation of the guidelines for
funds disbursal in this regard was given as the reason. The Ministry of Finance regulations
provides that spending pattern of the first quarter is criteria for getting eligible for
subsequent allocations on various schemes of the States. The Committee observes that
these guidelines may have adverse impact on other projects also and in such a case no
scheme could be properly implemented by the States. The Committee recommends that the
utilization certificates may be obtained scheme/project wise. If a particular scheme/project
is lagging behind in its execution, it should not be a reason to deny fund to the other
schemes/projects of the State. The Committee recommends that the guidelines on the
utilization certificates may be reviewed by the Ministry of Finance so that the proposed
projects may not be affected by the bottlenecks in the fund allocation norms. (Para 37)
The Committee observes that eventhough the rural tourism scheme was started in
the year 2002-03, the scheme has not made much progress so far. Only 186 projects have
been sanctioned since the inception of the scheme. The completion status is less than 50%
as only 90 projects out of 186 have been  completed during a decade, i.e., 2002-2012. Now
the scheme has been replaced with Rural Tourism Cluster scheme. The Committee observes
that undue delay in implementing the scheme is not acceptable. The Committee
recommends that the Ministry of Tourism may set the guidelines in such a way that the
scheme may yield results at the earliest. (Para 38)
The Committee recommends that Ministry of Tourism should ensure convergence of
resources and expertise through coordinated efforts with State/UT Governments and
stakeholders for an integrated and intensive development of tourism infrastructure in the
country through careful planning and execution while giving importance for improvement in
accessibility, environmental and other aspects. (Para 39)
The Committee notes that some projects identified in the years 2008-09, 2009-10 or
2010-11 are yet to take off like Aurangabad destinations of Maharashtra, Eco and Adventure
circuit, Arunachal Pradesh, Mubarak Mandi Heritage, Jammu and Kashmir etc. as no fund
allocations have been made for these so far. The Committee recommends that the
concerned State Governments may be encouraged to take the follow-up actions in these
regards and the funds may be granted in each case at the earliest. (Para 40)

The Committee notes that there was about one third cut in the allocations during the
RE stage for Domestic Campaign but even then it could not be utilized properly during
2012-13. The spending up to February 2013 was Rs. 55.62 crore out of the RE amount of
Rs.65 crore. The Committee feels the revision of rates and DA VP guidelines are not
convincing reasons for this. The Committee feels that Ministry should have been more
careful about this. The Committee also feels that the projects proposed by the Ministry need
to be innovative, interactive, and educative using mostly the print and electronic media. The
Committee appreciates the work done at the Delhi and Mumbai airports. The schools and

30
colleges throughout India can also be involved to spread awareness about tourism. The
school children may be given incentives to undertake tours and excursions by the Ministry
of Tourism which may ignite awareness of children and ultimately results in promotion of

The Committee feels that the initiatives of “Clean India Campaign” is a good idea
but the manner in which it has been proposed to be implemented leaves much to be desired.
As has happened in the case of National Culture Fund (NCF), under Ministry of Culture,

the desired activity perhaps has not been recognized as an activity under Corporate Social
Responsibility (CSR). And if it is so, the Ministry of Tourism should together with Ministry
of Culture, pursue this matter with the concerned Ministries for this purpose. The
Committee expresses its doubt about the success of such a campaign in the existing form.

In addition to this, awareness generation programmes also should be made about the
importance of keeping the tourist places and its surroundings clean. Such a campaign may
begin from our schools in which government organizations, private companies, local bodies
and State Governments and NGOs should also participate. (Para 53)

Survey of India, Port Trusts, ITDC etc to ensure development of tourism infrastructure like

disposal mechanism/re cycling plants etc., so that the efforts of the Ministry of Tourism in
their Clean India Campaign could be made a success. (Para 54)
OVERSEAS CAMPAIGN
The Committee notes that the Ministry has failed to utilize the fund allocated for
overseas campaign as they could spend only Rs.150 crore i.e. 56% of BE of Rs. 267 crore.

needs to be carefully utilized. Last year, the overseas campaign could not be launched till

th April, 2013. The Committee,
therefore, strongly feels that such unduly longer delays in finalizing schemes should be
avoided in future. (Para 58)

TSA for India does not give a clear picture in the absence of similar figures for other years

Posting in Overseas India Tourism Offices
India holds immense tourism potential of different kinds a better and variegated
than anywhere else. But, we have a long way to go in exploring that potential and
marketing effectively India abroad. Secondly, looking at the possible contribution from

31
tourism to our GDP and employment, role of our tourism offices abroad becomes of utmost
significance. The Committee is at a loss to see that working of our tourism offices abroad
leave much to be desired. Some are without heads and others are headed or manned by
persons having no experience in the relevant area. How can a person with no experience
be allowed to head our offices  abroad? The Committee fails to understand logic behind this
and is not surprised as to why the allocation for Overseas Campaign is not being utilized
properly. The Committee, therefore, recommends reconsidering the policy regarding
postings abroad and including an element of experience in relevant area in our guidelines

controversy regarding favouritism, etc. The Committee recommends that the DoPT rules for
deputation may be strictly applied on deputation to tourism promotion offices abroad.
(Para 64)
TRAINING
The Committee observes that for over several years, there has been a huge gap in
demand and supply in respect of trained manpower in tourism/hospitality sector. The
Committee has underlined this matter a number of times in the past also but it does not
find any significant improvement in this regard. There appears to be a lack of required
emphasis and urgency to fill up these gaps. More and more institutions and courses need
to be offered for manpower training and skill development in the tourism sector. The CBSP
scheme, no doubt, has very valuable components in it that seem to cover almost every
aspect of our requirements for Capacity Building and Training in tourism/hospitality sectors.
It appears that the Scheme is not being implemented with required emphasis. It needs
proper monitoring of and coordination with all the agencies involved at various levels. The
Committee emphasizes the need for having more training Institutions in hospitality and
related sectors in all parts of the country. (Para 71)
The Committee notes that Grants to IHM, the fund allocations seems to be going to
a limited number of States. In this case also adequate fund allocations need to be done to
those States which are having highest tourist density and potential yet to be explored.
(Para 72)
ACCOMMODATION INFRASTRUCTURE
The Committee notes that the funds under  the scheme Incentives to Accommodation
Infrastructure is not properly utilized in the previous years as the BE during 2010-11 was
Rs.10 crore and actual expenditure was only Rs. 50 lakhs. During 2011-12, also as against

revisited at the appropriate levels after finding out the reasons for low utilization in the

confidence in the scheme. (Para 79)

The Committee understands that NE states are generally prompt in getting their
tourism development schemes sanctioned and implemented. The Committee is also satisfied
that out of the 186 rural tourism projects, the NE States have secured 56 projects. The

32
Committee hopes that this may boost the tourism earnings in that Region. However, the
Committee is concerned about the fact that classification of cities in the NE Region has not

Computerization and IT
The Committee appreciates the emphasis given on the use of IT and Internet-based
options for providing updated information on India on a range of aspects needed by a
tourist. The Committee is aware of the ‘Incredible India’ and ‘Atidhi Devo Bhav’ websites
which have been created for the purpose. However, these efforts require to be made more
comprehensive and user-friendly. The Committee recommends that Ministry of Tourism may
coordinate with the State Governments, UT Administrations and important service providers
such as travel agents, tour operators, taxi operators, airlines, railways, airport operators,
local Police, hotels, shopping arcades, etc. so that tourists have all the information from
there. (Para 91)
TAXES THE TOURISM SECTOR
The Committee observes that the luxury tax on the hotel tariff ranges from 4% to
20% which may shoot up to 30% in the off season. Also the V AT on food items ranges from
5% to 16.84%. Tourist used to get discounts on the printed rates of room rent etc during
the off season but the tax should be paid on the original rate. The Committee recommends
that the tax concern of the tourism industry may favourably be considered. (Para 94)
The Committee observes that one of the major bottlenecks of tourism sector today
is the absence of uniform and rational Road Transport Tax structure in States and
multiplicity of taxes at inter-state borders. This is acting as an impediment to seamless
movement of tourist vehicles across State borders. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that tourist vehicles with all India permit may be taxed uniformly so that the bottle-necks
in the tax structures and the difficulties faced by tourists in crossing the state borders could
be addressed properly. (Para 95)
EVIRONMENT AND TOURISM
The Committee recommends that tourism activities should be based on scientific
carrying capacity and sustainability principles. As such, the normal peaceful living of the
wild life should not be disturbed by the tourism activities. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the ‘National Tiger Conservation Authority (Normative Standards for
Tourism activities and Project Tiger) Guidelines, 2012’ should strictly be adhered to, for an
eco-friendly tourism development in the country. (Para 100)
The hotel projects also need to follow the guidelines as regards conservation of
natural resources, increased use of recycled products, solar energy, water conservation like
rain water harvesting etc. The Committee recommends that Ministry of Tourism should

33
strictly monitor other measures like pollution control, introduction of non-CFC equipment
for refrigeration and air-conditioning, measures for energy and water conservation which
are to be undertaken by the hotels. (Para 101)
The Committee recommends that tourism activities at the protected areas should be
regulated as per the environment protection guidelines. No development is sustainable if it
is acted against the existence of nature. The Committee recommends that there should be
sincere efforts in environment protection while enhancing tourism facilities. (Para 102)
ITDC
The Committee was given to understand that occupancy in ITDC hotels has remained
40-50 percent even in the peak seasons. The Committee feels this is on low side and does
not know the reasons for this. ITDC has to function and compete with the professionally-
managed hotels in private sector. Therefore, it has to be competitive as regards services
offered by them. (Para 107)
The Committee noticed that the web sites of the Ministry of Tourism or the
Incredible India has no advertisement of ITDC hotels. The Committee feels that proper
links and advertisements about ITDC Hotels may be given in all the web sites under the
Ministry of Tourism. The Committee feels that ITDC hotels should also be marketed as part
of the overseas campaign. (Para 108)
The Committee notes that the financial performance of ITDC has improved during
the last two years. The Committee is hopeful that ITDC would keep its recovery path intact
in the coming years. The Committee appreciates ITDC on performing its social commitment
by extending its help organizing training of youth and contributing to the Clean India
Campaign. (Para 109)
The Committee recommends that light and sound shows have to be introduced in
other tourist spots of the country so that the famous tourist places may be made more
attractive to the visitors. Simulator based light and sound shows as available in the
Chardham Temple, Gangtok can be experimented in other parts of the country with
different themes. ITDC may take the initiative in this regard. (Para 110)
VISA ON ARRIV AL
The Committee notes the recent development in the visa-on Arrival Policy.  The
Committee is surprised to hear that because of non-availability of foreign language experts
of Japanese, German etc. the Ministry is seeking help from locals for the visa related
issues in the foreign countries. (Para 118)
The Committee recommends that our visa forms should be bilingual incorporating
the local language of the country. This will facilitate the tourists and increase their
confidence in visiting our country. The Tourism promotion offices should playa major role
in this regard. The Committee has reason to believe that many of our Tourism promotion
offices are filled up with deputationists who have no idea about tourism of India or the local
languages of the countries they are posted. (Para 119)
The Committee recommends that there should be clarity in issuance of inner-line
permits for the North-East. The Ministry of Tourism should take up the issue with the
Ministry of Home Affairs to clear all confusions in this regard. The Committee recommends
for immediate corrective measures in this regard. (Para 120)

34
NICHE TOURISM PRODUCTS
The Committee recommends for more cruise tourism projects at the viable states on
the lines of the initiative taken in Cochin Port. All the Major Ports, especially the
Mormugao Port has immense potential of cruise tourism which needs to be explored by the
Ministry of Tourism for development. (Para 123)
Adventure Tourism
The Committee notes the various measures taken in the Adventure tourism.  The
Committee also recommends that adequate trained people should be deputed in all the
adventure spots to monitor the participants and for rescue operations if required.
(Para 125)
The Committee feels that there is lot of potential in all these new tourism products.
The Ministry of Tourism should work on a detailed guide map on all these areas.
(Para 127)
SAFETY AND SECURITY
The Committee observes that safety and security is equally important, if not more,
for the growth of tourism sector. The Committee is concerned about the recent incidents
of attacks on tourists at different parts of the country. In addition to this, the Committee
noticed that even though safety guidelines are in place, these are less enforced and the
authorities are negligent towards these aspects until there are some incidents. All the State
Governments therefore may be persuaded/helped to set up tourism Police and prevent touts
and goons from various tourist destinations, airports, railway stations, etc. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the safety measures should be strictly implemented and
monitored at the different levels. The 24x7 infoline in foreign languages is a welcome step
up to attract the tourists. However, the Ministry should ensure that the people who are
manning it are capable and the service is available at ease. It should assist the tourists,
whenever they want. (Para 130)
GENERAL OBSERV ATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS
The Committee observes that the Tourism Ministry is mainly a fund-disbursing
agency. More than 90 per cent of its Plan allocation every year goes to four schemes
relating to infrastructure development, training assistance to institutes and publicity -
overseas and domestic. Once these funds are released, it seems it is left with the State
Governments and Union territories to utilise them. Nowhere is it reflected how the Ministry
is monitoring the utilisation of these funds and how they get feedback on whether the
States and Union territories are actually utilising these funds for the purpose for these
funds have been allocated. The Committee desires to know whether there is any robust
mechanism at different levels to coordinate these various aspects. (Para 131)
The Committee observes that sky rocketing of airfares and lack of government
control over it has recently affected the domestic tourist movement in the country. The
Committee also observes that higher user fee and ATF surcharges have eventually made the
air traffic journey un-affordable to many. The DGCA has taken some steps in this regard.
The Committee however, recommends that a more regular and strict watch on predatory
airfares being resorted by the airlines needs to done to prevent unreasonable airfares
especially during the peak seasons. (Para 132)

35
The Committee also observes that the rail travellers are facing problems due to shabby
coaches which are usually unclean with rodents roaming freely. The toilets are very dirty and
are seldom cleansed during the journey. Beggar menace and under quality food served are
other areas to be immediately attended. All these problems have made the train journey a
nightmare for most of the travellers and the tourists in particular. The Committee
recommends that Ministry of Tourism may take up the matter with Railway Board so that the
train journey may be made more attractive and comfortable to the tourists. (Para 133)
The Committee observes that we are not utilizing the full potential of tourism in
India. We always feel very sad about the fact that, probably, there is no country like ours
that has snow, hills to seas and beaches, adventure tourism, wildlife tourism, medical
tourism, etc., within the country. India has such a wide variety and destination. In spite of
that, the confidence does not seem to come that we are able to actually reach anyway close
to using our potential. (Para 134)

the Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha referred** the Bill as introduced in the Rajya Sabha on the
22
nd March, 2013 and pending therein, to the Committee on 25 th March, 2013 for examination and

3. The Committee took oral evidence of the Secretary, Ministry of Shipping and Chairman,
IWAI and other senior officers at its meeting held on the 18 th April, 2013 on various provisions of
the Bill.
4. The Committee wishes to express its thanks to the officers of Ministry of Shipping for

May 20 th, 2013 Department-related Parliamentary
Vaisakha 30, 1935 (Saka) Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture
* Published in Gazette of India Extraordinary Part-II, Section-2, dated 22 nd March, 2013.
**Rajya Sabha Parliamentary Bulletin Part-II No. 50787 dated 25 th March, 2013.

1
REPORT
The National Waterway (Lakhipur-Bhanga stretch of the Barak River) Bill, 2013 was
introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 22 nd March, 2013. On 25 th March, 2013, the Hon’ble Chairman,
Rajya Sabha, in consultation with the Hon’ble Speaker, Lok Sabha referred the Bill to the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture for
examination and report. (Annexure-I)
2. The Bill seeks to provide for the declaration of the Lakhipur-Bhanga stretch of the Barak
river in the State of Assam to be a National Waterway and also to provide for the regulation and
development of the said stretch of the river for purposes of shipping and navigation on the said
waterway and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
3. The Government had introduced the same National Waterway (Lakhipur-Bhanga stretch of
the Barak River) Bill in 2007 and the Bill was referred to the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture for examination and Report. The
Committee examined the Bill and presented its 130
th Report on 4 th March, 2008 to both the Houses
of Parliament. The Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha on 25 th February, 2009 and was sent to the
Rajya Sabha on 26 th February, 2009. The Bill, however, lapsed due to dissolution of the 14 th Lok
Sabha. As a result, the Government has brought again the same Bill before Parliament.
4. The Committee in its sitting held on the 18 th April, 2013, heard the views of the Secretary,
Ministry of Shipping, senior officials of the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) and the
Ministry of Law and Justice on the provisions of the Bill.
5. The Ministry of Shipping informed that total length of the Barak river system is 900 km.,
out of which, 524 km. passes through India, 31 km. is common boundary and the rest of 345
km. is in Bangaldesh. Out of the 524 km. in India, 403 km. upstream of Lakhipur is hilly and not
navigable. The navigable stretch is between Lakhipur and Bhanga. The Ministry of Shipping
proposes to declare the Lakhipur-Bhanga stretch (121 km.) of the Barak River as a National
Waterway. The entire waterway falls in the State of Assam. Infrastructural facilities currently
available on this waterway are not adequate for safe, convenient and sustained shipping and
navigation by large mechanized vessels. Therefore, the waterway is required to be developed by
providing adequate infrastructure for safe, convenient and sustained shipping operations. The
regulation and development of the proposed National Waterway under the control of the Union
Government for the purposes of shipping and navigation is in the public interest and declaration
to that effect has also been made in this Bill.
6. The Ministry of Shipping further informed that Inland Water Transport is an economic, fuel
efficient, environment friendly and employment oriented mode of transport. The role of the Union
Government is to regulate shipping and navigation on Inland Waterways declared by Parliament by
Law to be National Waterways. The responsibility and executive authority for development and
maintenance of all waterways other than those declared as National Waterways rest with the State
Governments.
7.   The Ministry has estimated that cargo traffic to the tune of 12.45 lakh tonnes will be
carried on the proposed National Waterway after its full development by the year 2018-19. This
traffic is expected to be handled at 4 terminals namely, Lakhipur, Silchar, Badarpur and Karimganj.
The identified cargo are bamboo and bamboo products, cement, coal, edible oils, provisions and
household items, fertilizers, iron and steel, paper and paper products, pulses, rice, stone boulder
and chips, sugar, tea and coffee, wheat, timber, wood, etc.

2
8. The Ministry of Shipping further stated that development of the river includes development
of the waterways for navigation, channel marking, construction of terminals, transit sheds,
installation of handling equipment, etc. The likely expenditure on the development of the 121 km.
stretch of the waterway would be Rs.123.3 crore (Rs. 85.3 crore for fairway development +
Rs.37.6 crore for terminal + Rs. 0.4 crore for setting up of office). Under phase-I, the waterway
stretch between Bhanga and Silchar (70 km.) will be developed in three years and thereafter the
upstream stretch of Silchar – Lakhipur (51 km.) will be developed after realistic assessment of
cargo potential on that stretch. Besides, annual maintenance cost of Rs.3.16 crore has also been
estimated for the maintenance of the proposed waterway and terminals.
9. The Committee was informed that the proposed Waterway No.6 will facilitate movement of
upto 300 tonnes vessel in this river. It will provide an alternative mode of transportation for
movement of commodities between ports of Haldia/Kolkata through Indo-Bangladesh Protocol route
for Transit and Trade and various hinterland cities namely, Lakhipur, Silchar, Panchgram, Badarpur
and Karimganj. It will also provide inter-country movement of goods between these hinterland cities
and that of Bangladesh. It will provide all weather connectivity with ports of Haldia and Kolkata
for not only Assam but also Mizoram, Tripura and Mainpur. This will be an alternative connectivity
of the North Eastern Region through Bangladesh and avoid the rail and road movement through
Chicken’s neck.
10. The Committee inquired about the differences between the current Bill and the Bill that was
introduced in 2007. The Secretary, Shipping informed the Committee that contents of both the Bills
are the same and the only difference is that the cost of development of Barak River has increased
in the present Bill. The likely expenditure on the development of the stretch of the waterway would
be Rs.123.3 crore.
11. The Secretary, Shipping also stated that when the earlier Bill was introduced, the project
was not approved by the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) of the Ministry of Finance,
Government of India. This Parliamentary Committee had pointed out in its Report about this and
had asked the Ministry to obtain the required approval. Accordingly, this time, the approval has
already been obtained from the EFC.
12.  The Committee notes that, at present, a lot of time and resources are being wasted
in transporting oversized cargo to the North-East. Waterways provide a hassle-free
movement of such cargo. Therefore, to have a water protocol with Bangladesh would open
immense possibility of cargo movement from India particularly from North Eastern region.
The Committee feels that therefore the Waterway should be extended up to Chittagong.
13. The Committee observes that the current Bill is the replica of the earlier Bill that
was introduced in 2007. That Bill was examined by this Committee and its 130
th Report
thereon was presented to Parliament. The Committee is happy to find that the required
approval of the Expenditure Finance Committee of the Government has been obtained this
time in pursuant to the recommendations of this Committee. Since, there is hardly any
difference between this Bill and the earlier Bill that was brought before the Committee in
2007, the Committee reiterates its concerns expressed and recommendations made in its
130
th Report on the National Waterway (Lakhipur-Bhanga Stretch of the Barak River) Bill,
2007. Those observations/recommendations of the Committee have been appended as
Annexure-II.
14. The Committee is surprised to see that even though the Committee had submitted
its Report on the previous Bill on 4
th March, 2008, the Ministry of Shipping has taken more
than 5 years to bring back the same Bill before Parliament. During this period, there has
been an escalation of about 34% in the project cost. The total estimated cost of
development of the waterway in the current Bill is Rs.123.30 crore as against Rs. 91.50

3
crore in the earlier Bill. The Committee expresses its anguish over this inexplicable delay
and hopes that the Ministry will give development of waterways the priority that it deserves.
15. While reiterating its recommendations contained in the 130 th Report, the Committee
adopts clauses 2, 3 and the Schedule of the Bill without suggesting any amendments
therein.
16. The Committee notes that the Parliament had passed the law to create Kakinada-
Puducherry canals with rivers Godavari and Krishna (1078 km.) as  National Waterway No.4
and the East Coast Canal with Brahmani river and Mahanadi delta rivers (588 km.) as
National Waterway No.5 in the year 2008. However, the Government is yet to take any
decision to operationalise these waterways despite the lapse of five years.
17. The Committee is at loss to find that two of our National Waterways No. 4 and 5 are
pending for the last five years to be operationalised mainly due to lack of funds. The
Government has brought a Bill for yet another waterway. It raises genuine apprehensions
about the operationalisation of this waterway.  The Committee, therefore, hopes that the
waterway No. 6, if passed, should not meet the fate of waterways Nos. 4 and 5. Funds for
waterways Nos. 4, 5, and 6 must be allocated at the earliest.
18. The Committee notes that out of the total 121 km. of the proposed National
Waterways No. 6, 70 km. (Bhanga-Silchar) will be developed under Phase-I, within three
years and the rest 51 km. (Silchar-Lakhipur) is proposed to be developed “after realistic
assessment of cargo potential on this stretch”. The Committee fails to understand why such
an assessment could not be made so far. Secondly, the estimated maintenance cost of
Rs.3.16 crore has not been factored into the estimated total expenditure of Rs. 123.3 crore
on the development of this waterway. This cost must also be provided by the Government
at the appropriate time.
19. The Committee notes that the Central Inland Water Transport Corporation (CIWTC)
has trained manpower and huge infrastructure meant for inland water transport. The
Committee is happy to note that the Government has taken a decision to merge CIWTC
and Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) so that the existing infrastructure of the
former can be effectively utilized by the latter. However, the Committee urges that the
terms and conditions of merger should be up to the satisfaction of the employees of
CIWTC. The Committee feels that the infrastructure generated at public cost should be
optimally used in the public interest and this should be the ultimate objective in the
Lakhipur-Bhanga Stretch of the Barak River. The Committee recommends to get the
merger process expedited.

4

The Committee notes that the Parliament had passed the law to create Kakinada-
Puducherry canals with rivers Godavari and Krishna (1078 km.) as National Waterway No.4
and the East Coast Canal with Brahmani river and Mahanadi delta rivers (588 km.) as
National Waterway No.5 in the year 2008. However, the Government is yet to take any
decision to operationalise these waterways despite the lapse of five years. (Para 16)
The Committee is at loss to find that two of our National Waterways No. 4 and 5 are
pending for the last five years to be operationalised mainly due to lack of funds. The
Government has brought a Bill for yet another waterway. It raises genuine apprehensions
about the operationalisation of this waterway. The Committee, therefore, hopes that the
waterway No. 6, if passed, should not meet the fate of waterways Nos. 4 and 5. Funds for
waterways Nos. 4, 5, and 6 must be allocated at the earliest. (Para 17)
The Committee notes that out of the total 121 km. of the proposed National
Waterways No. 6, 70 km. (Bhanga-Silchar) will be developed under Phase-I, within three
years and the rest 51 km. (Silchar-Lakhipur) is proposed to be developed “after realistic
assessment of cargo potential on this stretch”. The Committee fails to understand why such

5
an assessment could not be made so far. Secondly, the estimated maintenance cost of
Rs.3.16 crore has not been factored into the estimated total expenditure of Rs. 123.3 crore
on the development of this waterway. This cost must also be provided by the Government
at the appropriate time. (Para 18)
The Committee notes that the Central Inland Water Transport Corporation (CIWTC)
has trained manpower and huge infrastructure meant for inland water transport. The
Committee is happy to note that the Government has taken a decision to merge CIWTC
and Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) so that the existing infrastructure of the
former can be effectively utilized by the latter. However, the Committee urges that the
terms and conditions of merger should be up to the satisfaction of the employees of
CIWTC. The Committee feels that the infrastructure generated at public cost should be
optimally used in the public interest and this should be the ultimate objective in the
Lakhipur-Bhanga Stretch of the Barak River. The Committee recommends to get the
merger process expedited. (Para 19)

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS
The Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985 (82 of
1985) constituted the Inland Waterways Authority of India for the
regulation and development of inland waterways for the purposes of
shipping and navigation. The Central Government has already
declared a number of stretches of various rivers or canals as
National Waterways.
2. Allahabad-Haldia stretch of the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly
River, Sadiya-Dhubri stretch of the Brahmaputra River, Kollam-
Kottapuram stretch of West Coast canal and Champakaran and
Udyogmandal canals, Kakinada-Puducherry stretch of canals and the
Kaluvelly tank, Bhadrachalam-Rajahmundry stretch of river Godavari
and Wazirabad-Vijayawada stretch of River Krishna and Talcher-
Dharmra stretch of rivers, Geonkhali-Charbatia stretch of east coast
canal, Charbatia-Dhamra stretch of Matai river and Mahanadi delta
rivers have already been declared as National Waterways and the
Inland Waterways Authority of India has taken up the development,
maintenance and management of these National Waterways.
3. It is now proposed to declare the Lakhipur-Bhanga stretch
of Barak River in Assam as a National Waterway. Infrastructure
facilities currently available on this waterway are not adequate for
safe, convenient and sustained shipping and nagivation by large
mechanised crafts. Therefore, the waterway is required to be
developed by providing adequate infrastructure for safe, convenient
and sustained shipping operations. The regulation and development
of the proposed National Waterway under the control of the Union
for the purposes of shipping and navigation is in the public interest
and declaration to that effect has also been made in this Bill.
4. The Bill seeks to achieve the above objects.

OBSERV ATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
VIDE REPORT NO. 130 ON THE NATIONAL WATERWAY (LAKHIPUR-BHANGA
STRETCH OF THE BARAK RIVER) BILL, 2007
The Committee has consistently expressed its concern over the slow pace of
development of Inland Water Transport sector in the country. The Committee once again
notes that Inland Water Transport is one of the oldest, fuel efficient, cost-effective and
environment friendly mode of transport but unfortunately the potential of the sector
Inland Water Transport remains largely unexplored due to the indifferent attitude of the
Central and State Governments. The Committee observes that although the Department
of Shipping is committed to increase the share of Inland Water Transport in the country’s
total EXIM trade, still the waterways are not being utilized to their potential and remain
largely neglected and underdeveloped for want of required infrastructure namely fairways,
terminals and navigable aids, as a result, it has not reached at a threshold level to
become commercially viable. The Committee is of the view that with adequate
investments, policy framework and focused approach, the Inland Water Transport in the
country can be developed into a viable mode complementary to the rail and road modes.
The Committee is of the opinion that as the Government really intends to develop the
Inland Water Transport sector with fast pace to its full potential in the country it should
sincerely endeavor to provide institutional framework and minimize the procedural
bottlenecks besides providing adequate investments both from public and private
partnership primarily public investment in Inland Water Transport and to develop it to a
level where private sector feels confident to invest in this sector particularly in ownership
and operation of cargo and passenger vessels to Inland Water Transport mode. The
Committee, therefore, recommends the Government to provide institutional framework
and basic infrastructural facility for accelerated development of Inland Water Transport
sector in the country so as to increase the capacity of Inland Water Transport agencies,
commercialization of Inland Water Transport industries, increased cost recovery through
user charges and creation of a vibrant Inland W ater Transport sector in the country.
(Para 17)
The Committee notes with concern that Research and Development Studies facilities
especially in design of vessels and night navigation facilities and identification of
economically viable routes for development of Inland Water Transport sector has not been
given due consideration.  The Committee had already taken up the matter in its 121
st and
122nd Reports dealing with the National Waterway (Talcher-Dhamra Stretch of Rivers
Geonkhali-Charbatia Stretch of East Coast Canal, Charbatia-Dhamra Stretch of Matai River
and Mahanadi Delta Rivers) Bill, 2006 and the National Waterway (Kakinada-Pondicherry
Stretch of Canals and the Kaluvelly Tank, Bhadrachalam-Rajahmundry Stretch of River
Godavari and Wazirabad-Vijayawada Stretch of River Krishna) Bill, 2006 The Committee
again reiterates its view that Research and Development activities is the backbone for
success of any sector and recommends the Government to strengthen the Research and
Development facilities for the desired development of Inland Water Transport Sector in the
country by providing specific budgetary allocations. (Para 18)
14

15
The Committee notes that the proposed NW-6 can offer alternative mode of transport
vis-à-vis rail and road modes. The Committee also notes that the proposed NW will also
boost the rural economy and provide IWT connectivity for movement of commodities
between the Port of Haldia/Kolkata through Indo-Bangladesh protocol route for transit and
trade and various hinterland and Bangladesh besides decongestion of roads and fuel saving,
provide port-hinterland connectivity, better environment corridor and generate employment
among weaker sections and increase tourism activities in the region. The Committee
recommends that the existing Protocol routes connecting NW-1 & NW-6 and NW-2 & NW-
6 may be taken up with the Bangladesh on an expeditious way to convert these waterways
into international waterways for effective transportation of inter-country movement of goods
between hinterland cities and Bangladesh. But in the process the security concern should
not be compromised in any way. (Para 19)
The Committee observes that since waterways do not provide door-to-door service
independently, it is expedient that the waterways are connected with rail or road modes for
total transport linkages to the user. The Committee, therefore, recommends the
Government to improve the total modal mix of transport in the country and prepare the
road map for integrated transport policy to include IWT, Costal Shipping, Civil Aviation,
Road Transport and Highways and Railways. (Para 20)
The Committee notes with dismay about the inadequate repair facility being available
on the National Waterways. The Committee feels that IWT vessels once start plying in large
number on these waterways would require repair facilities on these waterways. The
Committee recommends the Department to prepare an action plan for meeting the growing
demands of repair and service facilities of IWT vessels on all the National Waterways.
(Para 21)
The Committee notes with anguish that no security personnel is being provided in
Sunderbans/Protocol routes in West Bengal by B.S.F./State Govt./IWAI. The Committee is of
the opinion that security is a prime concern and looked into seriously by making
commensurate security arrangement in Sunderbans/Protocol routes. The Committee
recommends the Department of Shipping to take up the matter of beefing-up of security
arrangement in the Sunderbans/Protocol routes with the Union Home Ministry so that
inadequacy of police deployment could be addressed in a big way. (Para 22)
The Committee is constrained to note that there is no updated Financial
Memorandum appended with the Bill and cost projections have been worked out based on
the year 2002. The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Government that after
declaration of NW-6 by the Parliament, the budgetary provision takes place. The Committee
is of the view that comprehensive planning and knowing the financial implication is a must
for the Government to provide allocation for development of this waterway. The Committee
therefore, strongly recommends the Department of Shipping to append the updated
Financial Memorandum based upon the individual project component of NW-6 with the Bill.
(Para 23)
The Committee is constrained to note that cargo transportation by Inland Water
Transport mode has not shown significant improvement on these National Waterways. The
Committee also expresses its displeasure over the fact that no comparative cost-output
evaluation for transportation of cargo through this alternate mode of transport has been
carried out by the Department. The Committee is of the view that such evaluation would
further establish the support of Inland Water Transport over other mode of transports.
Therefore, the Committee recommends that a detailed study should be carried out by the

16
Department in this regard and Department of Shipping should fix some realistic physical
target for cargo transportation year-wise for entire Eleventh Plan. (Para 24)
The Committee notes with dismay about the discontinuance of the Centrally
Sponsored Scheme for IWT development in the country by the Planning Commission. The
Committee is of the view that the decision of the Planning Commission to convert the
Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for IWT development into central sector scheme will
adversely affect the pace of development of Inland Water Transport in the country. The
Committee recommends the Department of Shipping to impress upon the Planning
Commission for the revival of the central sponsored scheme for overall development of the
IWT Sector. (Para 25)
Subject to the recommendations in the foregoing paragraphs the Committee adopts
clauses 2, 3 and the schedule without suggesting any amendments therein. (Para 26)
In clause 1(1) for the figure “2007”, the figure “2008” be substituted, consequently
the figure “2007” appears in the short title of the Bill may also be substituted with “2008”.
(Para 27)
In the enacting formula the words ‘Fifty-eighth’ be substituted by ‘Fifty-ninth’.
(Para 28)
The Committee recommends that the Bill be passed in its present form with formal
amendments. However, the Committee hopes that while implementing the provisions of the
Bill, the recommendations made by the Committee in the foregoing paragraphs will be given
due weightage so that the purpose of declaration of the proposed National Waterway should
not be defeated. The Committee also recommends that whenever necessary due
consultations and concurrence of the State Government of Assam be also taken in preparing
developmental plans and on other related issues for the proposed National Waterway .
